title: 2022 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 1
statement: Sets \(A, B\), and \(C\) satisfy \(|A|=92,|B|=35,|C|=63,|A \cap B|=16,|A \cap C|=51,|B \cap C|=19\). Compute the number of possible values of \(|A \cap B \cap C|\).

solutions.text: Suppose \(|A \cap B \cap C|=n\). Then there are \(16-n\) elements in \(A\) and \(B\) but not \(C, 51-n\) in \(A\) and \(C\) but not \(B\), and \(19-n\) in \(B\) and \(C\) but not \(A\). Furthermore, there are \(25+n\) elements that are only in \(A, n\) only in \(B\), and \(n-7\) that are only in \(C\). Therefore, \(7 \leq n \leq 16\), so there are 10 possible values.
